newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended near session lows on Tuesday, weighed down by caution ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting later and share placements from Henderson Land and COSCO Pacific.
The Hang Seng index closed 75.43 points lower at 11,546.70 after falling to a low of 11,538.76. Turnover was HK$10.38 billion, inflated by the two cash calls.

"Today's turnover is not very much at all counting those two placements. I think people are still waiting for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting tonight," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities.
Turnover on Monday was HK$4.86 billion.
Henderson Land placed 55 million shares at HK$64.00 per share. The stock closed down HK$2.25 at HK$64.00 on volume of 69 million shares.
COSCO Pacific placed 250 million shares at HK$6.20 each. Its shares ended on a loss of HK$0.20 at HK$6.35 on volume of 268 million shares.
James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said the market had held up quite well despite the placements.
"They have taken off the steam in the short term but it's pretty quiet around the market," he said.
Analysts said investors have discounted a 25 basis point rise in interest rates at Tuesday's Fed meeting and a hike could remove the uncertainty about interest rates in the market.
"But sentiment depends on whether (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan says anything else after the rate hike. People are waiting for a message," said Chan.
Shares in Hutchison Whampoa ended up HK$0.10 at HK$50.00, supported by talk of a covered warrant issue, brokers said.
The Philipines' Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority said its board of directors had again selected Hutchison Ports Philippines Ltd as the winning bidder to develop a container port terminal.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong shed HK$1.00 to HK$55.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.75 to HK$78.50.
Shares in HSBC Holdings fell HK$0.50 to HK$141.50 and Hang Seng Bank slipped HK$0.75 to HK$78.75.
Trading in Star Telecom shares was suspended pending an announcement. The stock closed at HK$2.875 on Monday.
